title: Initial forecast wind groups reduced strength gaps in rebuilt NHC 48-hour circle coverage in 2017-2025
abstract: We tested separate two-thirds track error radii below and above 64 kt of initial official forecast wind. Each target year used only the prior five years. In 2017-2025, the strong-minus-weak 48-hour coverage gap changed from 18.46 to -1.09 percentage points in the Atlantic and from 18.92 to 3.82 points in the eastern North Pacific. Proper quantile loss fell by 2.75% (95% storm interval -0.40 to 5.49%) and 2.25% (0.23 to 4.22%). Only the eastern Pacific primary score gain was clear. Secondary 24-hour gains were clear in both basins, but 72-120-hour intervals included zero. Initial forecast wind was recovered from best-track wind plus signed zero-hour error. All 73 checked archived OFCL initial winds matched exactly. Revised source records, selected storm stages, prior inspection of the archive and fixed-fit uncertainty limit inference. This tests rebuilt timed circles, not the full cone or impact risk. Code, aggregate results, source hashes and numerical checks are included.

display.caption: Earlier-year wind groups reduce strength gaps in rebuilt 48-hour circle coverage. The intervals describe paired storm-bootstrap loss reduction, with historical fits fixed.
